title: Viognier
description: A perfumed, full-bodied white that nearly vanished, saved by Condrieu and now grown worldwide.
L: Viognier gives full-bodied whites with apricot, peach, honeysuckle, violet and orange blossom. Acidity is low to medium, alcohol often high, 13.5 to 14.5%, and the texture oily and round. It's aromatic yet dry, a combination that can surprise first-time tasters.

Viognier is difficult to grow: low and irregular yields, prone to coulure, poor fruit set, and powdery mildew. By the mid-1960s, only about 14 hectares remained, mostly in Condrieu. Interest grew from the 1980s, and plantings spread to the south of France, California, Australia and beyond. Today there are over 15,000 hectares worldwide.
Low, irregular yields made it unprofitable
Poor fruit set and disease gave low yields, so growers abandoned it.

Look for medium to deep lemon or gold colour, an intense apricot and floral nose, and a full, round, oily palate with low acidity and warmth from alcohol. Compared with Gewürztraminer, it's more apricot than lychee, and less spicy.
Viognier typically has very high acidity.
Not true. Its acidity is low to medium, which gives it a round, oily texture.
Viognier gives apricot, honeysuckle and violet
It nearly vanished, with about 14 hectares in the 1960s
It's full, round and low in acidity

Viognier's home is the northern Rhône: Condrieu and Château-Grillet. It's grown in the Languedoc for IGP Pays d'Oc wines, and in California, Virginia, Australia's Eden Valley and Yalumba, and South Africa. Yalumba, in Australia, pioneered it there from 1980.

Viognier needs warmth to develop its perfume, but too much heat makes it flabby and alcoholic. It must be picked at full ripeness, when aromas peak; picked early, it tastes neutral; picked late, it loses acidity and gains bitterness. Like Gewürztraminer, the picking window is narrow.
What happens if Viognier is picked too early?
Its aromas develop late in ripening.

In Côte-Rôtie, up to 20% Viognier can be co-fermented with Syrah, though most use 2 to 5%. Co-fermentation stabilises colour, through a process called co-pigmentation, and adds floral lift. Australian producers adopted the idea for Shiraz Viognier.
What does Viognier add when co-fermented with Syrah?
Viognier is a white grape; it doesn't add tannin.
Viognier's home is Condrieu in the northern Rhône
It needs warmth and precise picking
In Côte-Rôtie it's co-fermented with Syrah

Condrieu is a small appellation in the northern Rhône, about 200 hectares, on steep granite terraces facing south and south-east above the river. The soil, a crumbly granite called arzelle, drains well. Condrieu must be 100% Viognier. The wines are rich, perfumed and dry, mostly drunk within five years.

Château-Grillet, within Condrieu, is one of France's smallest appellations, about 3.5 hectares, owned by one estate. It's a natural amphitheatre facing south. Its wines are more structured and age longer than most Condrieu. Since 2011, it has belonged to the Pinault family, owners of Château Latour.
It's one of France's smallest appellations, owned by one estate

Most Condrieu is dry, sometimes with oak for texture. Some producers make late harvest or sweet styles in warm years. Producers like Georges Vernay, who helped save the grape, and Yves Cuilleron are key names. Condrieu is usually expensive because of tiny yields and steep, hand-worked vineyards.
Condrieu is pure Viognier on steep granite
Château-Grillet is a tiny single-estate appellation
Most Condrieu is dry and best young
Know how long to keep it

Viognier's body and perfume suit rich dishes: roast chicken with apricots, pork, lobster, crab, creamy sauces, and mildly spiced Asian or Moroccan food. Apricot and ginger in dishes echo it. Avoid very acidic or delicate dishes, which make it seem heavy.

Serve at 10 to 13 degrees, not too cold, or its aromas close. Most Viognier is best within three years, when the perfume is fresh. With age, it loses aroma quickly. Château-Grillet and top Condrieu can age a little longer.
Why is most Viognier best drunk young?
Its fresh aromas are its charm, and they fade.
Try Viognier with a Moroccan chicken tagine with apricots. The fruit and spice match the wine's perfume.
Viognier generally ages as long as Riesling.
Not true. Low acidity means most Viognier fades within a few years.
Viognier suits rich, aromatic dishes and apricots
Most is best within three years
Which aroma is typical of Viognier?
Viognier's story runs from the Rhône to Australia.
In the 1960s only about 14 hectares of Viognier remained.
Yes. It was close to extinction.
White wines like Viognier have little tannin.
Viognier is best served at about ____ degrees.
Not too cold, to keep the aromas open.
Viognier is full, perfumed and low in acidity
It nearly vanished and was saved by Condrieu
It's best young, with rich, aromatic food
